answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, time-bound bond before it earns access to valuable tasks. The protocol caps concurrent exposure per bond and slashes it when independently verified fraud appears. An attacker who tries to forge a nebula of aliases must fund a separate bond for every identity and risks losing each one, so the cost grows linearly with the attacker's scale. Honest agents recover their stake after the challenge window, while a small attacker cannot hide behind a ledge of cheap usernames.
